sol.text:
Zhuang Liu: I think for ninety-nine percent of the tasks we care about today—coding, writing, research, planning, even many kinds of reasoning—the language-level world model may already be enough, or at least enough when combined with tools and feedback from the environment. You don't need to simulate every pixel or every physical interaction in order to answer an email or write a program, right?

But if you want the model to act reliably in the physical world—robotics, driving, manipulating objects—or even to generate long, physically consistent videos, then I think you do need a much more fine-grained world model. Language compresses away many details that usually don't matter to us, but those details can become essential when you need to predict exactly what happens next. So I wouldn't say every task needs the same world model. It depends on the abstraction level of the task. For most digital tasks, language plus tools may take us very far; for embodied intelligence, I think vision, temporal experience, and interaction with the world will be necessary. Yeah.
